sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant/injured seeking enhancement of compensation being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded under judgment and award dated 5.4.2023 passed in MVC No.2204/2021 on the file of learned Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Bailhongal1.
2.

Sri. Hanamant R Latur, learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant met with road accident on 23.3.2021 and sustained three major fractures, but the Tribunal contrary to the evidence on record has assessed disability at 18% to the whole body, which is on the lower side.
He further submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal under other heads is on the lower side and seeks to enhance the same appropriately by allowing the appeal.

3. Per contra, learned counsel Sri. S.S. Koliwad for the respondent/Corporation supporting the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal submits that the award of compensation by the Tribunal under each heads is just and proper and does not call for enhancement.
Hence, he seeks dismissal of appeal.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the appeal papers meticulously.
5.

The material on record discloses that in a road accident occurred on 23.3.2021, the appellant sustained undisplaced fracture 'Tribunal', for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:11383 of femoral condyle right, wedge compressed fracture of T12 vertebra, wedge compressed fracture of L4 vertebra.

Taking note of the same and considering oral testimony of PW2, who treated the appellant, this Court is of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to re-assess the disability of the appellant at 20% to the whole body.
Insofar as assessment of income of the injured by the Tribunal at Rs.14,250/- per month is unaltered.
There is no dispute with regard to age of the appellant i.e., 48 years and appropriate multiplier of 13.

Thus, loss of future earnings of the appellant is recalculated as under:
Rs.14,250 x 12 x 13 x 20/100 = Rs.4,44,600/-
6.

This Court on appreciation of evidence available on record is of the considered view that the Tribunal awarded meager compensation under other heads, which is modified as under:
 Pain and suffering Rs. 60,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs. 40,343/-
 Loss of amenities Rs. 40,000/-
Food, nourishment, attendant charges conveyance etc. Rs. 20,000/-

 Which is rounded off to Rs.6,47,700/-

7. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER a) Appeal stands partly allowed.

NC: 2024:KHC-D:11383 b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the appellant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.6,47,700/- as against Rs.5,39,983/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

d) The respondent/Corporation shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) On such deposit, the same shall be released in favour of the appellant on proper identification.
f) Registry to draw modified award accordingly.
g) No order as to costs.
